To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we describe for the first time the anatomical mapping of ghrelinergic system in goldfish and the first daily expression rhythms of both genes in fish.

we have mapped the distribution of ghrein and its receptor in the brain and gastrointestinal tract in goldfish, and we have shown that the expression of these molecules is regulated daily in these tissues, suggesting a possible link between the ghrelinegic and circadian systems.
ghrelin and its ghrelin receptor (GHSR) were mapped in the brain and gastrointestinal tract in goldfish, and that their expression is regulated by daily cycles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the physiological role of ghrelinergic system in fish, and provides a solid basis to further explore ghrelin and its related peptides as potential targets in aquaculture.
the identification of the anatomical distribution and possible daily expression of prepro-ghrelin and Ghs-R1a ghelin receptor subtype in brain, pituitary and gastrointestinal tract of the goldfish.
the identification of the anatomical distribution and the characterization of the daily expression of ghrelin, a gut-brain hormone, in goldfish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ghrelin is a multifunctional hormone that plays important roles in fish, and that the ghrelin system in fish is regulated by a circadian clock.
preproghreline and ghs-r-1a expression is rhythmic in hypothalamus, pituitary and gastrointestinal tract, with a possible role in the control of food intake and energy metabolism.

ghrelin and its ghrelin receptor are widely distributed in the brain and gut, and that both genes are regulated in a diurnal manner in goldfish, which may suggest that the ghrelin system plays a role in the regulation of feeding behavior in this species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ghrelin and ghelin receptor are expressed in the gastrointestinal tract and hypothalamus of goldfish, with a daily variation in the hypothalamo-pituitary axis.
ghrelin and ghr-receptor are expressed in the brain and gut of goldfish, with the most important expression in the hypothalamo-pituitary region and in the mucosa of the digestive tract, respectively.
ghrelin and ghrelins receptor are present in goldfish brain and GI tract with daily rhythms in mRNA expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ghrelin and its receptors may be involved in the control of feeding and metabolism, and in the regulation of the circadian clock in goldfish.

ghrelin and ghelin receptor are widely expressed in the brain and gut of goldfish, with the most prominent expression in the gastrointestinal tract and hypothalamus, respectively, and that their expression levels display a daily rhythm in the brain and in the gut, with the acrophases occurring at nighttime.
goldfish ghrelin and its receptors display a similar pattern of expression as in mammals.
